rules.coverage_note: A label entry: a key whose immediate owner is `labels` and which lies somewhere under a `metadata` key. Stated by ancestry rather than by an exhaustive list of qualified names, because a pod template's metadata sits at `spec.template.metadata` in a Deployment, `spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.metadata` in a CronJob and `spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].metadata` in a StatefulSet -- and at a depth nobody can enumerate inside a CRD instance.

A annotation entry: a key whose immediate owner is `annotations` and which lies somewhere under a `metadata` key. Stated by ancestry rather than by an exhaustive list of qualified names, because a pod template's metadata sits at `spec.template.metadata` in a Deployment, `spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.metadata` in a CronJob and `spec.volumeClaimTemplates[].metadata` in a StatefulSet -- and at a depth nobody can enumerate inside a CRD instance.

gaps: Helm and Kustomize are not executed; only the authored YAML/JSON documents retained in the repository are indexed, so a templated value is carried through as the template text

omega-yaml states no document fact, so several documents separated by --- in one file are one path: the same-file joins that pair a kind with its metadata.name cross-produce across the documents of a multi-document file, and an object declared there can be minted under a kind belonging to a sibling document
a Kubernetes object with no metadata.name (a Kustomization, a raw List) is not minted as an object; its file is still a KubernetesManifest
an RBAC subject is keyed by name alone: subjects is a sequence of mappings and omega-yaml emits no per-item fact, so the sibling kind of one subject cannot be told from another's
